pointers.sentence: The admin knows only the models it is told of, and must be told before its URLs are built: `AdminSite.get_urls` makes them from the registry as it then stands ([The admin's URLs: `AdminSite.get_urls` and `AdminSite.admin_view`](site-urls.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.get_urls`).

It adds the site to `all_sites`, a weak set of sites, which the admin's system checks go through ([The admin's checks: `check_dependencies` and `ModelAdminChecks`](checks.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.__init__`).
A single model, an instance of `ModelBase`, is made a list of one, and each model is taken in turn (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.register`):
So is a model with a composite primary key; the documentation calls the admin's support for such keys work still to come (`docs/topics/composite-primary-key.txt`).
The auth application's admin module registers `User` whatever `AUTH_USER_MODEL` names (`django/contrib/auth/admin.py:UserAdmin`).
Made without it in a run, the class said it lived in `django.forms.widgets`, the module of its metaclass's `__new__` (`django/forms/widgets.py:MediaDefiningClass.__new__`).

`AdminSite.unregister` deletes each model it is given from the registry, raising `NotRegistered` for one that is not there; `AdminSite.is_registered` asks the registry; `AdminSite.get_model_admin` returns the model admin or raises `NotRegistered` (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.unregister`, `django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.get_model_admin`).

`AdminSite.unregister` deletes each model it is given from the registry, raising `NotRegistered` for one that is not there; `AdminSite.is_registered` asks the registry; `AdminSite.get_model_admin` returns the model admin or raises `NotRegistered` (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.unregister`, `django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.get_model_admin`).

Applied to a class, it refuses with `ValueError` a call that named no model, a site that is not an `AdminSite`, and a class that is not a subclass of `ModelAdmin`; then it passes the models and the class to the site's `AdminSite.register` and returns the class unchanged: in harbour's admin module ShipAdmin names the class, and the instance lives only in the registry (`django/contrib/admin/decorators.py:register`).

`AdminConfig.ready` does what `SimpleAdminConfig.ready` does, registering the admin's system checks, then calls `autodiscover`, which imports, by `autodiscover_modules`, the module `"admin"` of every installed application that has one, with the default site as the registry to restore if an import fails ([Importing by name: `import_string` and `autodiscover_modules`](../utils/importing.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/apps.py:AdminConfig.ready`, `django/contrib/admin/__init__.py:autodiscover`).

`AdminConfig.ready` does what `SimpleAdminConfig.ready` does, registering the admin's system checks, then calls `autodiscover`, which imports, by `autodiscover_modules`, the module `"admin"` of every installed application that has one, with the default site as the registry to restore if an import fails ([Importing by name: `import_string` and `autodiscover_modules`](../utils/importing.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/apps.py:AdminConfig.ready`, `django/contrib/admin/__init__.py:autodiscover`).

`SimpleAdminConfig` registers the checks and discovers nothing, for a project that registers with a site of its own and imports its admin modules itself, as the documentation says (`docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).

`django.contrib.admin.site` is a `DefaultAdminSite`, a `LazyObject` whose `DefaultAdminSite._setup` imports the dotted path the admin application's config gives as `SimpleAdminConfig.default_site` and calls what it names ([Lazy objects: `LazyObject` and `SimpleLazyObject`](../utils/lazy-objects.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:DefaultAdminSite`).

`ModelAdmin.__init__` keeps the model as `ModelAdmin.model`, its `_meta` as `ModelAdmin.opts` and the site as `ModelAdmin.admin_site`, then `BaseModelAdmin.__init__` merges in `BaseModelAdmin.formfield_overrides` ([The admin's forms: `get_form` and `formfield_for_dbfield`](admin-forms.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.__init__`).

`ModelAdmin.__init_subclass__` warns when a subclass sets `ModelAdmin.list_select_related` to `True`, deprecated in 6.1 ([The change list: `changelist_view` and `ChangeList`](change-list.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.__init_subclass__`).
A model admin's options are class attributes, with defaults on `BaseModelAdmin`, which inlines share, and on `ModelAdmin` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin`).

`BaseModelAdmin.get_queryset` gives the model admin's pages their rows: the default manager's queryset, ordered by what `BaseModelAdmin.get_ordering` returns, by default `BaseModelAdmin.ordering`, when that is not empty, else by the model's own (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.get_queryset`).

`get_object` converts the key from the URL by the `to_python` of the primary key, or of the field `"_to_field"` names, and returns the one matching row of the queryset, or `None` when the key does not convert or no row matches (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_object`).
